nodes.label: Record conventions enforced by something, not merely tidy
nodes.norm_label: record conventions enforced by something, not merely tidy

nodes.label: Minimal output to protect the caller's context window
nodes.rationale: The explorer returns file paths and one line of context per finding, with no recommendations or quality opinions, because every token it returns lands in someone else's context window and the caller — not the explorer — holds the judgment.
nodes.norm_label: minimal output to protect the caller's context window

nodes.label: reviewer-architecture lane
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-architecture (model opus, effort xhigh)

nodes.label: One owner per concern (lane ownership boundary)
nodes.rationale: A lane raises only what its own card owns and stays silent on things it notices that belong to other lanes, because duplicate findings cost the lead triage time and dilute the single-owner guarantee that makes the lane set coverable.
nodes.norm_label: one owner per concern (lane ownership boundary)

nodes.label: An empty findings array is a correct result
nodes.rationale: Padding is forbidden because a lane that always finds something gets ignored, and a permanently ignored lane is worse than one that occasionally misses a finding.
nodes.norm_label: an empty findings array is a correct result

nodes.label: Evidence and cause honesty
nodes.rationale: `evidence` records what was actually seen and `cause` records whether the diff introduced it; `direct` is never marked for something reasoned to but not pointed at, inferred evidence alone can never block, and `stale` findings are recorded rather than fixed. Triage weights these fields and cannot re-derive them.

nodes.label: Establish the architecture in force before judging
nodes.rationale: Run the tier procedure — discovered documents, then the project reference graph, then convention inferred from three or more existing examples — and set `evidence` from the tier reached, so that a convention merely inferred can never block. Then ask, per changed type, what single kind of work it owns and whether the diff gave it a second one.
nodes.norm_label: establish the architecture in force before judging

nodes.label: .claude/review/conventions.md accepted-deviation ledger
nodes.rationale: Deviations already examined and deliberately accepted are recorded here; anything in it is an accepted decision and never a finding, so reviewers read it before judging placement.

nodes.label: Read-only reviewer enforcement via disallowedTools
nodes.rationale: Every review lane denies Edit, NotebookEdit, and the mutating shell and git commands (rm, mv, cp, sed, tee, truncate, git add/commit/push/checkout/restore/reset/revert/clean/stash/rebase/merge/worktree), so a reviewer can write only its findings and log files.

nodes.label: reviewer-artifacts lane
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-artifacts (model sonnet, effort high)

nodes.label: Run the generate-and-diff check rather than reason about currency
nodes.rationale: Where a generate-and-diff, restore, or schema check exists the lane runs it and reports the command and its output as evidence, because whether a generated artifact is current is a fact to be observed, not inferred.
nodes.norm_label: run the generate-and-diff check rather than reason about currency

nodes.label: reviewer-deadcode lane
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-deadcode (model sonnet, effort high)

nodes.label: Establish reachability by search; deduplicate by family
nodes.rationale: Reachability is established by searching and reading call sites rather than assumed, and findings are collapsed to one per obsolete workflow rather than one per member it already names, so triage sees a decision rather than a list.
nodes.norm_label: establish reachability by search; deduplicate by family

nodes.label: reviewer-lite-correctness consolidated lane
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-lite-correctness (model sonnet, effort high)

nodes.label: Consolidated-lane attention drift
nodes.rationale: The characteristic failure of a merged lane is finding one interesting problem early and never covering the rest, so a consolidated lane must work through every concern its card lists before writing anything, and its log must show it looked at each.

nodes.label: reviewer-lite-security consolidated lane
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-lite-security (model sonnet, effort high)

nodes.label: A Critical in lite security escalates to the full loop
nodes.rationale: The lane must state a Critical plainly in its one-line return, because the lite loop's one-way escalation to the full loop is decided from that report rather than from the findings file.
nodes.norm_label: a critical in lite security escalates to the full loop

nodes.label: reviewer-lite-structure consolidated lane
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-lite-structure (model sonnet, effort high)

nodes.label: Separation of concerns first
nodes.rationale: The structure sweep is ordered deliberately: for each changed type, ask what single kind of work it owns and whether the diff gave it a second one — before architecture placement, before standards, before surplus and dead code. Separation of concerns outranks the other structural considerations, so it must be spent attention on first rather than reached last.

nodes.label: reviewer-lite-tests consolidated lane
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-lite-tests (model haiku, effort high)

nodes.label: reviewer-minimalism lane
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-minimalism (model sonnet, effort high)

nodes.label: Removal findings held to a higher bar than addition findings
nodes.rationale: A guard the brief asked for is not bloat, so the brief is checked before anything is raised; and because a removal finding proposes deleting working code, it must clear a higher bar than a finding that merely objects to an addition.
nodes.norm_label: removal findings held to a higher bar than addition findings

nodes.label: reviewer-requirements lane
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-requirements (model opus, effort high)

nodes.label: Write down the expected diff before comparing
nodes.rationale: The lane records what it expects the diff to contain from the brief alone before reading the diff, then compares — an anchoring guard. Each requirement must be pointed at by line; a requirement that cannot be pointed at is treated as missing.
nodes.norm_label: write down the expected diff before comparing

nodes.label: reviewer-security lane
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-security (model opus, effort xhigh)

nodes.label: Trace untrusted input end to end; assume the caller is hostile
nodes.rationale: Every untrusted input is traced from entry to use and reachability is checked before anything is raised; the caller is assumed hostile and not who they claim to be. Exploitation against live systems is forbidden — the check is analytical, not active.
nodes.norm_label: trace untrusted input end to end; assume the caller is hostile

nodes.label: reviewer-standards lane
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-standards (model sonnet, effort high)

nodes.label: Documented rules only
nodes.rationale: The standards document is the sole source of style rules: if a rule is not written there it is not a finding. A reviewer who believes a rule is missing says so in its log rather than enforcing an unwritten rule as a finding.

nodes.label: coding-standards skill
nodes.rationale: Preloaded into the sidekick implementation agents and into the review lanes that own style, so that implementation and review are judged against one identical rule set.

nodes.label: reviewer-technical lane
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-technical (model opus, effort xhigh)

nodes.label: Error paths are where reviews find the most and tests cover the least
nodes.rationale: Changed behaviour is traced end to end including what happens when a dependency throws, times out, or returns partial results, because that region has the highest defect density and the lowest test coverage.
nodes.norm_label: error paths are where reviews find the most and tests cover the least

nodes.label: reviewer-tests lane
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-tests (model sonnet, effort high)

nodes.label: Mutation testing in a scratch worktree
nodes.rationale: The question is not whether a test exists but whether it would fail if the code were wrong, and the only way to settle that is to break the code and run the test. The mutation happens in a scratch worktree — an exact copy on a detached commit not on any branch — which the lead discards whole, so the mutation is left in place and there is no cleanup and no risk to the reviewed tree. Where no scratch path was given, the reviewer records `mutation testing: unavailable` rather than improvising a mutation elsewhere.
nodes.norm_label: mutation testing in a scratch worktree

nodes.label: Primary working tree immutability and the lead's digest check
nodes.rationale: Concurrent lanes read the primary tree and the lead commits it, so a write there means the diff that ships is not the diff that was reviewed. The lead takes a content digest before spawning reviewers and compares after they drain, which detects a write and costs the round a rerun — but the stated reason not to write is that it corrupts the review, not that it would be caught. The digest checks the result rather than enumerating causes, because no permission list catches every spelling.
nodes.norm_label: primary working tree immutability and the lead's digest check

nodes.label: reviewer-ultra-adjudicator
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-ultra-adjudicator (model sonnet, effort high)

nodes.label: Adversarial pair reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Two reviewers examine the same lane on opposite assumptions, blind to each other, and a third produces the lane's single authoritative findings file — nothing downstream reads the halves. Resolution rules: both raised it, keep at the higher severity; only defence raised it, keep unless the code contradicts it; only prosecution raised it, decide against the code and the defence log — dismissed with a reason that holds means drop, dismissed with a reason that does not hold means keep, never reached means decide on the code alone. Every kept finding must be independently verified and its `evidence` set from the adjudicator's own check, because adjudicating from the two reports alone is arbitrating between summaries, which is how a confident wrong finding beats a hesitant right one. Severities are picked, never averaged, and no new finding may be smuggled in as an adjudication.

nodes.label: The dropped list as pair calibration
nodes.rationale: The adjudication log's dropped list is the most useful thing the adjudicator produces: it is how the lead learns whether prosecution is running too hot or defence too quiet, and that ratio is the main signal to watch across runs. The log also carries a `coverage` verdict — both logs substantive, one thin, or both thin — so two silent reviewers with thin logs are reported as an uncovered lane rather than a clean one.
nodes.norm_label: the dropped list as pair calibration

nodes.label: reviewer-ultra-defence
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-ultra-defence (model sonnet, effort high)

nodes.label: Precision-optimised review posture
nodes.rationale: Assume the change is correct and the author knew what they were doing; raise only what can be demonstrated by pointing at the line and stating the trigger. Try to explain the code before condemning it — look for the caller that already validates or the invariant held elsewhere — and prefer the narrower claim. The counterpart already covers recall, and duplicating that leaves nobody covering precision, collapsing the pair into two reviewers with the same blind spots. The trap: precision is not agreeableness — waving everything through fails more dangerously than flagging everything, because the adjudicator reads silence as evidence of correctness.

nodes.label: The defence log matters more than its findings
nodes.rationale: The log must record what was examined and concluded fine and the reason it is correct, not merely that it was looked at. When the adjudicator sees a prosecution finding defence did not raise, the log is the only thing distinguishing 'considered and dismissed' from 'never reached' — and those lead to opposite adjudications. An empty findings array is normal for defence; a sparse log is not.
nodes.norm_label: the defence log matters more than its findings

nodes.label: Never recommend removing a security control or invariant guard unattributed
nodes.rationale: A reviewer may not recommend removing a permission check, security control, idempotency guard, or lock ordering without stating what else establishes that invariant — the burden is on the remover to name the replacement.
nodes.norm_label: never recommend removing a security control or invariant guard unattributed

nodes.label: reviewer-ultra-prosecution
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-ultra-prosecution (model sonnet, effort high)

nodes.label: Recall-optimised review posture
nodes.rationale: Assume the change is broken and something is there to find. Because the adjudicator discards what cannot be supported, the cost of a weak finding here is low and the cost of a missed real one is high, so the threshold for raising is deliberately lowered — unproven suspicions still go in, marked `evidence: inferred` and `confidence: low`. Failure is hypothesised actively: for each changed behaviour, ask what input, ordering, or state would break it and work back to the code. Tests are assumed inadequate until the one that would catch the concern is found, and severity is never softened to seem reasonable.

nodes.label: A lower threshold is not lower honesty
nodes.rationale: Marking a suspicion as `direct` is singled out as the one thing that corrupts adjudication, because the adjudicator weights evidence heavily and cannot re-derive it. `confidence: low` is expected from prosecution and costs nothing. Volume is not licence to review other lanes.
nodes.norm_label: a lower threshold is not lower honesty

nodes.label: reviewer-ultralight
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-ultralight (model sonnet, effort high)

nodes.label: Nine-item all-concern sweep
nodes.rationale: One reviewer covers, in fixed order and without reordering or stopping early: requirements, correctness, error paths (given their own item rather than folded into correctness), separation of concerns (explicitly not to be compressed), placement, standards, security, tests, and surplus. The risk is not capacity — eligibility rules keep anything substantial away — it is attention drift, and the per-item log verdict for all nine items is the only evidence the lead has that the sweep happened rather than stopping at item three. A reviewer that reports it could not cover an item causes the lead to escalate, which is the correct outcome and not a failure.

nodes.label: Authz or untrusted input found here means the change is in the wrong loop
nodes.rationale: The ultralight loop's eligibility rules should have kept authorization and untrusted input away entirely; finding either is evidence the routing decision was wrong, so the reviewer must say so prominently rather than simply reviewing it.
nodes.norm_label: authz or untrusted input found here means the change is in the wrong loop

nodes.label: reviewer-verify
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: reviewer-verify (model opus, effort high)

nodes.label: Four final verification questions
nodes.rationale: Exactly four questions are in scope before a PR: does the final diff still do what the brief asked; does the validation match what was touched; did the required checks actually run or is there a stated blocker; do the deferred findings have concrete reasons. The advisor deliberately has not seen the review rounds and must not reconstruct them — the risk it exists to catch is that cumulative repairs drifted from the original intent. A green suite that never exercised the changed path is not evidence, and an unrun check recorded honestly as blocked is acceptable while an unrun check nobody mentioned is a finding.

nodes.label: Verification is not a re-review
nodes.rationale: Style, architecture, and security findings are out of scope here because those lanes have already run and duplicating them restarts a loop that was correctly terminating. A gap is worth one targeted fix, not another full round, and because this is the last gate before a human sees the work, a false alarm costs more than it would mid-loop.

nodes.label: sidekick-heavy implementation worker
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: sidekick-heavy (model opus, effort xhigh, maxTurns 80, memory project)

nodes.label: Verify the constraint that drove the escalation
nodes.rationale: The escalation buys reasoning for one specific constraint, so that constraint must be identified and verified deliberately — by test, argument, or measurement, with the method named — rather than assumed satisfied. On a retry the previous attempt's diff is read first to understand why it failed. Depth goes into the code and the verification, not the write-up.
nodes.norm_label: verify the constraint that drove the escalation

nodes.label: Push back on the brief, but do not expand scope
nodes.rationale: If a constraint is unsatisfiable, two constraints conflict, or the brief's implied approach is the reason it is hard, stopping with the specific argument is worth more than a compliant implementation that quietly violates something. Pushing back is explicitly not the same as redesigning unprompted.
nodes.norm_label: push back on the brief, but do not expand scope

nodes.label: Stop rather than guess when a decision appears
nodes.rationale: The brief is complete by construction, so an unsettled design decision, a change requiring restructuring rather than editing, or an instruction that does not fit the file are all signals the routing was wrong. Stopping early with a precise description of what was hit is the correct outcome and cheaper than a wrong guess. The worker is exhaustive rather than clever — if a pattern applies to all call sites, every call site is grepped and changed.
nodes.norm_label: stop rather than guess when a decision appears

nodes.label: sidekick default implementation worker
nodes.source_location: frontmatter name: sidekick (model sonnet, effort high, maxTurns 60, memory project)

nodes.label: Treat the brief as a spec
nodes.rationale: Every stated constraint, edge case, and definition of done is honored literally — an O(1) constraint means restructuring until it holds, not shipping O(n). Exploration is limited to what the task needs, the approach is not redesigned and scope is not expanded, and the worker never commits because the lead reviews and commits.
nodes.norm_label: treat the brief as a spec

nodes.label: A precise blocker report is a success, not a failure
nodes.rationale: When a task turns out to need judgment the brief does not settle — a design decision, an unstated tradeoff, a constraint conflicting with existing code — the worker names the decision and stops rather than resolving it, so the lead can re-brief or route to a stronger tier. Guessing hides a routing error inside working-looking code.
nodes.norm_label: a precise blocker report is a success, not a failure

nodes.label: Project agent memory for repo conventions
nodes.rationale: The implementation workers carry `memory: project` and check it for already-established conventions before starting, then record durable learnings afterwards — project structure, naming and style conventions, test layout, build quirks, recurring review feedback, invariants discovered, why an obvious approach fails here — so future runs need less exploration.
nodes.norm_label: project agent memory for repo conventions
